Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power

Source: R/estimateSensitivity.R
estimateSensitivity.Rd

From the variance fits (estimateVariance()), computes the analytic standard error of the two-group log2 fold-change contrast per gene (SE^2 = 1/sum_A w + 1/sum_B w, w = 1/(1/mu + phi), phi the dispersion with the condition in the design), the minimum detectable effect at the target power and FDR, and the power at the primary target effect. Summarises to the comparison's expected recall at targetLFC: the mean per-gene power at the target over the testable genes, i.e. the share of true effects of that size the test is expected to detect if they are spread like the testable genes. callComparisons() calls a comparison Adequate when its expected recall reaches defaultThresholds()$sensitivity (0.5). On OneK1K with known injected effects it tracked the observed recall per comparison (slope 1.0), whereas the sensitivity fraction (the share of genes whose MDE clears the target at the target power, still reported) under-predicts it (E4c). Uncalibrated in the MVP (calibrate = FALSE).

Usage

estimateSensitivity(
  variance,
  targetLFC = 1,
  power = 0.8,
  fdr = 0.05,
  pi1 = "discoveries",
  alphaFixed = NULL,
  calibrate = FALSE
)

Arguments

variance

The list returned by estimateVariance().

targetLFC

Primary target absolute log2 fold-change for the call. Default 1.

power

Target power. Default 0.8.

fdr

Target FDR. Default 0.05.

pi1

Fraction of true positives that maps the FDR to a per-gene threshold: "discoveries" (default) estimates it per comparison as the fraction of genes the comparison's own DE test calls at fdr; a number fixes it for every comparison (falls back to 0.05 for a comparison whose fit has no p-values).

alphaFixed

Optional fixed per-gene significance level. NULL (default) uses the pi1-mapped level alone; a number makes the call use the stricter of the two (the larger MDE).

calibrate

Reserved; must be FALSE in the MVP.

Value

A data.frame, one row per comparison, with target_lfc, the pi1 and per-gene alpha used, expected_recall (the summary behind the call), sensitivity_fraction, median_mde, median_mde_fdr, median_mde_fixed (NA without alphaFixed) and median_power.

Details

The FDR target is mapped to a per-gene significance level through the fraction of true positives pi1 (Jung 2005), capped at fdr (BH never tests a gene at more than the FDR level). BH's realised per-gene threshold scales with the fraction of genes it calls, so no fixed pi1 suits every contrast: a sparse contrast (male vs female in blood, realised threshold ~1e-4) makes a fixed 5% optimistic, a dense one makes it conservative. By default (pi1 = "discoveries") each comparison uses its own fraction of BH discoveries, R / m from the DE test of the chosen method at fdr (floored at 1 / m), so power is evaluated at the threshold BH actually uses there. On OneK1K with 0.5-20\ of genes injected as DE and on male vs female it was the best calibrated of the rules tested (E4b).
